How to update an article after a game change, and how to record what changed.

== Update the fact, then the metadata ==
Change the actual figure/behaviour in the article body first. Then update {{tl|Article status}}'s <code>version</code> and <code>reviewed</code> fields to reflect when and against what version you checked — never leave stale defaults after making a substantive change, even a small one.

== When Live and Legacy diverge ==
If a change only applies to Live and Legacy keeps the old behaviour, don't just overwrite the old figure — state both explicitly in the prose ("On Live, X; Legacy retains Y") and fill in the <code>legacy_differences</code> field on {{tl|Article status}}. See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Content Style Guide]] for how to phrase this.

== Recording the change: Patch history ==
For anything more than a one-line note, add a row to that article's {{tl|Patch history}} table (create the section near the bottom, in the same position as {{tl|Engineering nav}}, if the article doesn't have one yet):
<pre>
{{Patch history|
! Update !! Date !! Change
|-
| [[Trailblazers]] (Update 3) || 2025-04-30 || Colonisation economy reworked.
}}
</pre>
Link the Update name to its own Game Update article where one exists ({{tl|Game update infobox}}) — that link is what lets <code>Special:WhatLinksHere</code> on the Update's own page answer "which articles did this update affect," with no separate per-update category needed. If the article's own <code>version</code> field also names that update, link it the same way — see [[Trailblazers]] and [[Colonisation]] for a worked example of both sides of this connection.

== Use <code>recent_changes</code> for a one-line pointer ==
If a change is genuinely minor and doesn't need a full Patch history entry, the optional <code>recent_changes</code> field on {{tl|Article status}} is enough — a short sentence, not a table.
